persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.emotion: torn between love and being unseen
understanding.bridge: The life your father keeps describing is not the one you are living. What he sees is a fear he has, and it is his, not your measure.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told who you are by your father to standing in the person you are, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being told who you are by the person you love, and the pain of not being seen.
week_beats.story: A son who questioned his father's fear and stood in his own truth shows you what that looks like.

understanding.core_struggle: A student who loves film is being told by his father to do an MBA, and he feels his father does not see him at all.
understanding.mirror: Every night the same fight, and in the next room the sound of your mother crying.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being told who you are by the person you love most, and the pain of watching someone you love not see you at all. I keep fighting with my parents.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a fear they have, their picture is their smallness, not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture starts to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A young man of learning whose father dismisses his path, who stood in his truth before his family and was proven right in time.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
verse.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
verse.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna sits on the battlefield, his bow dropping from his hand. He tells Krishna that his mind is confused about what is right and that his nature is stricken by weakness. He asks Krishna to tell him plainly what is best. He admits he does not know, and he asks to be taught. This is the moment clarity begins. It is not about having the answer. It is about admitting you do not know and asking for help.
verse.for_you: Your father tells you who you are every night over the MBA, and your mother cries in the kitchen. You are confused about what is right. You do not have to know the whole answer right now.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
verse.sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
verse.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
verse.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verse.why: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

prasang.title: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.
prasang.story_hook: Mandodari took her husband's hand and led him somewhere the ministers couldn't hear.
prasang.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

verse.meaning: Tulsidas is watching Ravana's court. Ravana's ministers are flattering him as Ram's army arrives. Mandodari has just taken Ravana aside and begged him to return Sita before it is too late. But Ravana only laughs at her fear and walks into court. There, his ministers tell him exactly what pleases him. Tulsidas says that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verse.for_you: Your father is telling you a story about who you are. But it is his fear, not your truth. You are living a different life than the one he keeps describing.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that doing your own work, even if it is flawed, is better than doing someone else's work perfectly. The work that fits your own nature, done as an offering, brings no wrong to you. This is the truth underneath the daily struggle.
verse.for_you: You sit with your books and the noise of the fight is still in your ears. Your father wants an MBA, but your nature is in films. Do not let him make you feel that your own path is a failure. Offer your honest work to your own truth.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.line: Friend, enemy, stranger, relative, saint or wrongdoer: the one who sees all with an even mind stands highest.
verse.translation: One who is even-minded towards well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked, excels.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Even-minded is not naive; you can treat someone fairly and still keep a boundary.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna how to stand firm. He says that the person who stays calm when people praise them, blame them, love them or hate them has reached the highest level of wisdom. This means you do not have to let other people's anger or approval decide how you feel about yourself. You can choose to be your own steady friend instead of your own worst critic.
verse.for_you: Your father's anger is his own fear, not your worth. When they raise their voice tonight, stay even-minded. You do not have to fight back to prove you are seen. Just be your own steady friend.

verse.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Brihaspati counsels Indra on how to hold authority among difficult people.
verse.sanskrit: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः / मातीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव
verse.line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
verse.translation: People look down even on the gentle, and they shrink from the harsh. Do not be only harsh, do not be only soft: be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is.
verse.misuse: Firmness here means clarity, not cruelty.

matched.label: I need to set boundaries with family

verse.meaning: Brihaspati speaks to Indra about ruling over people who are hard to manage. He explains that people will take advantage of someone who is too soft and will fear someone who is too harsh. The one who stands highest is the one who knows the moment and acts with balance. This is not about being cruel or weak. It is about knowing when to hold your ground and when to let the other person breathe.
verse.for_you: Your father's anger is his fear, not your measure. When he speaks tonight, let your voice stay steady. You do not have to shrink or shout. Just say what you need, and let the room hold the silence after.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is telling Nidagha how a person who is free inside moves through the world. The work is right in front of them. They speak gently. They read what is in the other person's heart. They do not push or pull. They do not cry for what is lost or beg for what they want. They do the work that is there. They treat everyone the same. They do not sink. They stay calm on the inside while they are busy on the outside.
verse.for_you: Your father is afraid. You do not have to match his fear. You only have to do your own work. Speak your truth gently. Then let the next step be your work. You do not sink.

story.title: Father and son go back to school
story.story_hook: When his son came home stumped, Uddalaka did something unusual for a famous teacher.
story.summary: A patron asks young Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer. He asks his father, who admits he does not know either and suggests they both go to the patron as students. Chitra welcomes Uddalaka for his humility.
story.lesson: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.

anchor.speaker: Shvetaketu and Uddalaka Aruni
anchor.setting: A patron asks Shvetaketu a question he cannot answer; he goes to his father.
anchor.sanskrit: स होवाच नाहमेतद्वेद हन्ताचार्यं प्रच्छानीति स ह पितरमासाद्य पप्रच्छेतीति स होवाचाहमप्येतन्न वेद सदस्येव वयं स्वाध्यायमधीत्य हरामहे यन्नः परे ददत्येह्युभौ गमिष्याव इति ॥
anchor.line: 'I don't know either,' the father told his son. 'Let's both go and learn, as students.'
anchor.translation: He said, 'I do not know this. Let me ask my teacher.' He went to his father and asked. The father said, 'I too do not know it. We have studied the Veda and take what others give us. Come, let us both go.'
anchor.why: A parent who says 'let's learn together' teaches more than any answer.

script: Every night over the MBA, your father tells you who you are. Your mother cries in the kitchen. You are torn between loving them and feeling completely unseen. That is a heavy thing to carry right now.
Arjuna sits on a battlefield. He has dropped his bow. He is weeping and refuses to fight. Krishna is right there with him. Arjuna said:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः, यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्.
In plain words: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.

Arjuna admits he does not know the right path. He asks to be taught. This is where clarity begins. It is not about having the answer. It is about admitting you do not know and asking for help. This is easier said than done because it takes courage to stand in your own confusion and let someone else see it.
You do not have to know the whole answer right now. You only need to admit to yourself that your father's picture of you is not the one you live in. Let that truth sit with you for a moment.

depth.life: Your father tells you who you are every night over the MBA, and your mother cries in the kitchen. You are confused about what is right. You do not have to know the whole answer right now.
depth.points: Arjuna, a warrior, collapses in tears on the battlefield because he is confused about what is right. He admits his mind is clouded and his nature is stricken by weakness. He does not pretend to know the answer. He asks Krishna to teach him plainly, saying he is ready to learn and is his student.
depth.practice: Pick one moment today when your mind is quiet, and say out loud, I do not know what is right yet.
depth.question: What is one small thing you can admit you do not know?
